utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We gather there are procedural matters that counsel wish to raise. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has dealt in private session because of the nature of some of the material with three motions. The first concerned motions by the Prosecution for protective measures in respect of witnesses that are to be called in this case. For reasons which we have given, we -- the Chamber has decided against granting protective measures in respect of both of the applications. The first is not a victim, and the justification advanced does not come within the Rules. The second witness is a victim, but the essential issue is the identity of that witness. That identity has been the subject of public knowledge fully available on the Internet in a report that is public for sometime and has also been the subject of earlier evidence in this trial, which has not been protected. And essentially in that factual situation, the Chamber does not see that there is a factual justification for attempting at this late stage to impose some form of protective measure. The third motion was of a -- a different kind entirely, and concerned an application by the Boskoski Defence for access to minutes of a meeting within this Tribunal held in 2002. The Chamber proposes to defer its decision in respect of that application because of the significance of some of the issues raised and will publish a written decision in due course. You call the next witness, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I do that, I must inform the Chamber that when the witness informed me earlier this morning that he requested these measures, these protective measures, I asked the witness what his position would be if such measures were denied. And the witness declined to give me a response. I am perfectly willing to call the witness into the courtroom unless the Chamber wishes to take a short recess and allow me to consult with the witness on his position. But I'm perfectly willing to call the witness in if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you should call the witness, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then the Prosecution calls Mr. Blagoja Toskovski, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Mr. Toskovski. You're able to hear me with a translation, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Toskovski, I should tell you -- first of all, apologise to you for the delay. You've been kept waiting while we've been dealing with some matters. One of those was an application by the Office of the Prosecutor on your behalf for some protective measures. I should tell you that the Chamber has been forced to conclude that it has no power under the Rules in your case to grant protective measures. So there are no protective measures in respect of your evidence. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, is your name Blagoja Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you a citizen of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is your ethnicity Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what is your current occupation and title?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: At this moment, I work as the deputy director of the public security bureau within the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, when did you join the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I joined the Ministry of the Interior for the first time in 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in August of 2001, what was your position?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In August 2001, I was at the post of inspector in property and other offences in the department for internal affairs, Cair, within the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in that post as inspector, can you tell us, please, just in general what were your responsibilities at the time, in general terms.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: At that post, my responsibilities -- or actually, my job description would entail, have entailed, any property offences, any crimes related to property, motor vehicles, any forgery related to motor vehicles, as well as forgeries of other documents, as well as offences in the area of damaging of certain facilities, installations, so that would also comprise fires caused by various reasons. So that would be it briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Toskovski, I'd like to ask you to turn your mind, please, to the events of 10, 11, 12 August 2001. Do you recall that on the 10th of August, 2001 eight Macedonian soldiers were killed in a mine explosion at Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you working that day? It was a Friday.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I was working, until 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you hear about the mine explosion that morning when you were at work?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what, if anything, the Ministry of Interior decided to do in response on that Friday, the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm not aware of anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And then can we turn, please, to Sunday, the 12th of August, if you can turn your mind to the events of that day. Were you working on Sunday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We worked in shifts, so I was on duty on that day as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately what time you started work that day?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: At 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall if anything in particular was happening that morning in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We received an information that -- that at that moment there were police activities in the village against terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall who told you about this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, it was the head of the operative unit who informed us in brief summary that such events were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what was the name of the head of your operative unit?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Ljupco Josevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And that day, Sunday, the 12th of August, where did you spend that day at work? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was stationed at the premises of the operative unit. They are in the same building where the Police Station Cair is. So I was in the offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Recall seeing any police officers around the Cair police station that day?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: There was the regular -- the ordinary security as well as on any other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So at the time during the day, 12th of August, there was normal police activity going on in Cair police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the morning, yes, you can say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anyone was arrested later that day?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you describe how you know this, how do you know that persons were arrested?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Somewhere during the day I received an order from my superiors to go to the Mirkovci police station, and I was told that there were detainees there, persons brought in, and this is why I needed to investigate the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And at that time were you told where the arrested persons had been detained?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that they were brought in in relation to the activity in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall when you received these instructions to go to the Mirkovci police station, do you recall whether you reacted positively at first to those instructions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you inquire - if you can recall - why you were being sent to Mirkovci to do this investigation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think that I did ask, since there are several inspectors in the police station, and this is why I asked the question whether it would be me only or should anyone else go as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you thought about other people, were you speaking about -- were you thinking about other particular inspectors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, whether any other inspector should go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what was the response? Can you tell me who you inquired -- well, what was the response to your concern?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I asked the -- both heads of the department for internal affairs, Krstevski Ljubomir and of the operative unit, Ljupco Josevski. They told me that I needed to go to observe the situation and then to call them on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there was something you were supposed to prepare?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In what sense? I do not understand the question. To prepare what?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were there any documents, if you can recall, that you were supposed to prepare as part of your work?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean before I went there? I don't understand you. Which documents are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did your superiors indicate to you that it was necessary to prepare anything at that time, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, it follows, it's the ordinary course of work. They just mentioned that should there be any elements of a criminal offence, I should then take all measures, activities, to clarify the case, and, if needed, to then prepare criminal reports, one or several, depending.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you then go to the Mirkovci police station on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately what time you arrived at Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely. I believe it was around 1600 hours, maybe later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it help you to refresh your memory if I show you part of a statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor some time ago, where you described this -- the hour? Would that assist you to recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we have copies of the English and Macedonian version of the witness's statement. If we could ask the usher's assistance, please, to distribute those. And if a Macedonian version could be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, if you could turn, please, to what is paragraph 15 in the version in front of you. Do you see paragraph 15?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at the last two sentences of paragraph 15, it says the following: "Being asked, I tried to remember the exact time but I'm not sure anymore. I can say that when I arrived at the station," and that's Mirkovci, "it was dark. I think it was after 2000 hours." Does this help to you refresh your memory about the time, the approximate time you arrived at Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think it was somewhat earlier than 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Any idea how much earlier?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: After giving this statement, I gave further thought, and recalling, I'm thinking from 1600 to 1800 hours, within this period of time I arrived in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. When you arrived at the Mirkovci police station, can you recall whether you saw any colleagues that you knew there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the police station, there were uniformed persons and two female colleagues which I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we start with the uniformed persons, can you -- can you describe what kind of uniforms these persons were wearing?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: At that time, mostly these were camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And do you know from what institution or what ministry these persons wearing the uniforms came from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Part of them were from the police station of Mirkovci. I do not know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The two persons that -- two female colleagues who you knew, did they -- do you know why they were there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believed they were also there on assignment, to observe the situation because one of them was an analyst; and the other worked in the unit for minors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did both of these -- both of these female colleagues, they were working within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You then mentioned that you saw a number of people wearing uniforms, some of whom you knew were police officers from Mirkovci. How were you dressed at that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have been thinking about this question also during the last time we talked about this when I was given this written statement, and then I stated that I was not sure whether I was wearing civilian clothing or a uniform. I've been thinking about this further, and I came to the conclusion that on that day I was in uniform after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you recall seeing someone in the Mirkovci police station who was wearing something a bit unusual?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall seeing a person in Mirkovci police station wearing a mask?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think there were persons with masks and camouflage uniforms, for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall what kind of mask it was?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: A standard one used by the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you arrived, did you see anyone in Mirkovci police station dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Other than my female colleagues, I don't think having seen any other persons in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, can you recall the name of the person who was the commander of the Mirkovci police station in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I know him, but I cannot, at this moment, remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, to assist you, could you take a look, please, at paragraph 19 of the statement that's in front of you, the first two sentences of that paragraph. It says --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "The first thing I did was I spoke to the commander of the police station, Slavko. He was in his office." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does that help to refresh your memory about who the commander was?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, correct, this is the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall whether Slavko was present when you arrived, the commander known as Slavko was present when you arrived at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think he was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you speak to him? Did you speak to Slavko?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I had a short conversation in connection with the person that were brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall where you and the commander Slavko were when you spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall where the commander's office was or is at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is located on the first floor to the right, straight down the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you said that you had a short conversation with Commander Slavko. Can you recall what the two of you discussed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: We discussed about the persons who had been brought in and detained, and I requested information about their whereabouts, where they were, and I informed him that I have an order to see those persons and to undertake further necessary measures as provided by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall what the response of Commander Slavko was?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe he briefly responded that the persons are in the ground premises, that I can do my work, and that he would secure everything he needed to secure from his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did Commander Slavko -- can you recall whether Commander Slavko told you about other persons who were speaking with the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He said that inspectors from the state security office had already spoken to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after you had this discussion with Commander Slavko, what did you do after that; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I saw two persons, inspectors, allegedly from the state security, whom I did not know. They gave me a list with the identification of the persons that were held, and a list with cases with -- and a list with objects that were found in their person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, you said that these persons were inspectors allegedly from the state security. Are you referring to the state security bureau of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What made you think that these persons were from the state security bureau?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is how they identified themselves to me and told me they had previously spoken with the persons that were detained. They established their identity and that I can continue further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by "you can continue further," just so that the record is chore, does that mean you could continue to do your work there in the Mirkovci police station. Is that the point of what they said?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely this is so. I have my work to carry out, since his scope of work had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, at some point did the gentlemen from the state security bureau leave the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think, yes. I did not see them after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And after you no longer saw the gentlemen from state security, do you recall what you did after your discussion with them? Do you recall whether you contacted anyone?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I requested to go to the persons and to see the detained persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say you requested to do this, can you recall who you made this request to?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not mean this literally. I requested for uniform assistance, a person accompanying me to the areas where the persons were held.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before you made that request, you recall whether you received any more instructions from your superiors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, because I had still not been in contact with them after having come to the station. I did not have sufficient information to hear my superiors and to inform them of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And when you say you asked for -- you requested uniform assistance, a person to accompany you to the areas where the arrested persons were held, and did a uniformed policeman then accompany you to that area?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the way that things are done in the station. A uniformed police officer accompanies me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was it your intention at that -- let me step back for a moment. Was it your intention at that time to begin to interview the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I had no intention. I was not thinking anything and I could not think about anything until I had seen the persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So then where did you go? What part of Mirkovci police station did you go to; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I recall. Down the interior staircase, I went to the ground, the underground part of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is there a particular room or part of the police station where the arrested persons were?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: The person accompanying me in the police station told me that the persons are below and took me there. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall ever going to a garage?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is not a garage. Sometimes it is perhaps used for parking a vehicle, because it is on the same level as the side part of the ground of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if we can refer simply to the area where the arrested persons were, who did you see when you arrived in that area; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not understand your question well enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you go to the area where the arrested persons were being held, on the ground floor at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And who was present in that area? Can you recall who was there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: The persons who were detained were there and internal police security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Internal police security. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It means security from the police station, because these are the inside, the internal premises of the police station. There was also external security, security in the courtyard of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this internal security and the external security, this was all -- was this performed by members of the police station, police officers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they were all in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you arrived at this area, did you see the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how did the arrested persons look when you saw them in the garage; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: The detained persons had certain injuries on their faces. This is why prior to undertaking any additional measure, I called my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which superiors would those be?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Krstevski and Josevski, both heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what did you discuss with Mr. Krstevski and Josevski, at that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I reached Krstevski, and I told him that I am requesting that an ambulance be sent immediately in the police station so that to allow me to take any further action onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you receive the permission that you asked for?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The chief Krstevski said that he would immediately organise and dispatch such a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. Might this be an appropriate time to take the first break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has prepared some exhibits, copies of exhibits, that it will be showing to the witness today, and we have copies for the Chamber and, I believe, for the Defence as well. And if I could ask the court officer's assistance, please. If can we can see what is Exhibit P257 on e-court, please. And, Your Honours, this is at tab 2 of the binder that you've just received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Toskovski, if you can turn to tab 2 and underneath the English version, you will find a version in your own language. Before we took the break, Mr. Toskovski, you mentioned that you were requesting an ambulance be sent immediately to the police station. And this document in front of you, it says: "Official Note, 1187," it's dated the 12th of August, 2001. It's submitted by Suza Zengovska from the Cair internal affairs division, Mirkovci police station. And it's about medical examination of detainees. And in the second paragraph, you'll see that it talks about how the detainees at Mirkovci, ten persons, were

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: established. Do you see that, Mr. Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "But the doctor said there was no need for any of the persons to be transferred to a health centre or hospital." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Is that your recollection of events when -- what happened when the ambulance came?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. But if you allow me to clarify it. This is a note that I see for the first time and from it one can see that it is Dr. Karamanovski, Gjorgi. During the night, ambulance cars arrived on several occasions to the Mirkovci station so that we monitor the health status of the detainees and so that we can, if needed, take certain actions, if there is any need to have someone transferred to a medical institution. The first ambulance, when it arrived, on it was a female doctor. And here I can see that this is a male doctor, a man.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Did I cut you off or is that enough?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: That would be it. This is what I wanted to say, that it happened several times that ambulance came.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Tell me, why was it necessary for ambulances to come to the Mirkovci police station that same night on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I requested this, principally, in order to avoid some misunderstandings later.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: That no proper medical assistance was rendered, although the visible injuries were in the nature of light injuries or at least this is how they appeared, from visual observation. I'm not an expert in any internal injuries that might have been there.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So just to understand your testimony, when you saw these ten detained persons at Mirkovci, and you noticed they had some light injuries, and you requested that an ambulance come to examine these persons and subsequently, the ambulance came with the female doctor, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And then that female doctor left. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: But then you're saying several times during the night it was necessary for ambulances to return and check these arrested persons again.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did anything that you're aware of happen to these ten detainees between the first visit by an ambulance and a doctor and the subsequent visits?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I state absolutely nothing has happened to them. They had the same injuries as from the first moment when I arrived at the station.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Then why did they have to be examined again and again?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: That was done upon their request. Some of the persons requested to be rendered medical assistance again, and this is why the ambulances came several times.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You said a couple of minutes ago, you told the Chamber it was due to your request, that you made subsequent requests. So I'm trying to understand what is correct.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, probably it was a misunderstanding. Of course, I was the one calling for the ambulance, but that was done upon previous request of some of the injured people when they insisted. So I was the one deciding upon that and I would call an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, can you look at the first paragraph, please, of this document and I'll read it to you: "At 2000 hours on 12 August 2001, ten persons, residents of the village of Ljuboten, were brought to the Mirkovci police station after they had been taken into custody by a special unit of the Ministry of Interior at the check-point in the village of Ljubanci." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you know which special unit or units are being -- of the Ministry of the Interior that's being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to any members of such units who had taken these ten persons into custody?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I spoke to the person who took them over and brought them to the police station Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to come to that in a minute. Mr. Toskovski, eventually during the night of the 12th to the 13th of August, did you speak to each of these ten arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to them all.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you spoke to them individually or in groups?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I spoke with each of them individually.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And can you recall where you had these individual conversations with each of the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I ran the interviews in a room adjacent to the one where the detainees were held.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So that was, again, down on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And can you recall why you decided to speak with these persons in that room down on the ground floor rather than in some other part of the police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, there were several reasons for it. Firstly, it was in the immediate vicinity. It was more practical and it was closer to have the interviews there. Secondly, in the offices on the upper floor of the station there were several authorised officers, and I didn't want to find myself in a situation that some of the detainees of the persons brought in would -- would be -- I didn't want to allow for the possibility that any of detainees is additionally injured on the road towards those offices. Those are the main reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, do you recall what specifically you were worried about, in terms of additional injuries? Do you recall what danger you were concerned about?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I was thinking in terms of general, unpredictable risk, in a situation where there is a strong presence of police forces and the situation was tense.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You say there was a -- a strong presence of police forces and the situation was tense. What were you worried about that might occur; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I said I was thinking of prevention. I didn't want to allow room for any additional incident.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Would it help you to refresh your memory on this topic, if you take a look at the statement you gave, Mr. Toskovski? Take a look at paragraph 27, please, of your statement. Do you see paragraph 27?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: It says: "Being asked if I spoke with all of them," the arrested persons "I say yes, I spoke with all of them, one by one. Near that garage there is another room. At this place I spoke with them. We did this for practical reason, not to bring them up. There was also a danger that police officers would attack them. That is how I estimated the situation; I have seen the anger of the policemen." Do you see what I've just read?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Does that help you to refresh your memory about what your concerns were on that evening, your professional concerns?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I just think that this is a different version of what I had already said, a modification of phrasing maybe, in the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Is what you said here in paragraph 27 correct, Mr. Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think that this sentence is overly strong. I don't think I said it like this, that they will be attacked. This is too strong a word, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: In the English version it says: "There was also a danger that police officers would attack them." Would that be correct? Is that what you told the investigator back in 2004?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I think there was a risk of some incidents. Attack is too strong a word. I couldn't have said it like that.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall, Mr. Toskovski, whether anyone was with you -- actually, let me step back for a moment. You said there was a risk of some incidents that evening. Were you concerned that -- about the risk that some of the arrested persons might be injured or further injured, if such an incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What are you referring to? What kind of concern?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: What incidents were you worried about?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, incidents lighter in character than what is written here. Attack may be --

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Maybe some attempt of something. This was my thinking.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall when you were speaking with these ten individuals one by one whether anyone was with you at the time; can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I was accompanied by authorised officers, uniformed police officers throughout the time.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. Before you began speaking with these arrested persons, do you recall whether you received any information explaining the circumstances of the arrests?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I received a verbal information, as I said, also from the people in charge of state security and from the police station commander that the persons who were there then were brought into custody from the actual scene of the events in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you receive any information that one or more of these persons might have been in possession of weapons or ammunition when they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I received such information, and I said earlier that there was a list containing the identity of the persons and the objects found on them.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And when you spoke to these arrested persons individually -- sorry, let me step back for a minute. Apart from the conversation that you had and the list that you received about the identity of the persons and the objects that were found on them, apart from that did you ever receive any arrest reports regarding the circumstances of the arrests?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: When you spoke with these persons in that room near the area where they were being held, approximately how long would you speak with them; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you mean with all of them or with each of them individually?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I apologise. Thank you for setting me straight. My question should be: For each individual discussion, approximately how long would one last; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I recall that the interviews would last in the average 10 to 15 minutes, with each of the persons.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. And did you confront these arrested persons with information that weapons and ammunition had been seized from them when they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. To each of them individually, I presented the information that I had, and I asked them whether they were accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did any of these individuals agree that this information was accurate?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No one agreed that the information was accurate. They all denied it, although they did confirm that they have seen that there was combat going on, but allegedly they themselves did not participate in it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you made a record of these interviews?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we can show the witness, please, what is exhibit number P54, pages 105 to 106, and this is a document that's at tab 3 of the binder that you have.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: If you could turn, Mr. Toskovski, to what is tab 3 in the materials in front of you, to the Macedonian version, please. Mr. Toskovski, this is an Official Note, number 535. At the top it says: "Submitted by Toskovski, Blagoja," and then the date 13 August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And is that your signature at the bottom of the second page?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So did you draft this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I prepared that.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So you prepared this note on the 13th of August, right? It would have been a Monday.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, probably. I don't recall it now. Yes, the next day.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And you see there the names there of ten persons there. In the first paragraph I think there's a typo because it says: "I had official conversations with nine persons who were withdrawn from Ljuboten village by the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia."

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Ten.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Exactly. If you look two paragraphs below you use the number ten; do you see that? The third paragraph, it says ten; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the first paragraph I see it is written ten.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Then the English translation has an error. It should say ten. Thank you for catching that. The third paragraph says: "All of them, the above mentioned ten persons were present in Ljuboten village during the combat activities of the security forces and they were trying to pull out of the village in direction to its exit. The above named persons stated that shots of weapons could be heard everywhere in the village." Then it says: "Actually, there was a fight between the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And then it says: "The persons above mentioned stated that they noticed many terrorists fighting with fire-arms in their hands and that as of themselves they did not take part in combat activities but they wanted to run out of the Ljuboten village. Actually, some of them wanted to surrender to the security forces because they were not men who would participate in fights." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Below that we see a list of weapons and ammunition that were found at the site where the accused were apprehended, according to your note; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And then at the end of the list of weapons and ammunitions we see a sentence that says: "Weapons and ammunition seized from the above mentioned persons at the site where these were found was undertaken with a certificate for seized objects." So, is it correct to state that during your discussions with these ten persons you also produced some seizure certificates related to the weapons and the ammunition that were allegedly in the possession of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I did issue certificates on seized objects.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: We'll look at a few of those in a few minutes. Mr. Toskovski, do you know if anyone ever tested the weapons that were allegedly seized at Ljuboten for fingerprints?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: They were handed over to the crime technicians for further investigation and analysis of any such prints, if they were to be found.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you or anyone else direct that fingerprint samples be taken from the hands of the ten persons who were detained at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not order anything like this. It is possible that as part of the procedure this was done when the paraffin glove was taken.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: But you're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not know about this. However, if I would be allowed to clarify, even without taking a fingerprint there at the very place of events, we have such prints for each in -- of each citizens in our ID list of citizens. Therefore, the comparison can be done even without taking additional fingerprints.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. And do you have any knowledge whether such fingerprint comparison between prints on the weapons and ammunition and the prints of the arrested individuals was done?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is obligatory when weapons are handed over for expertise. If fingerprints are found, I do not know. However, this is an obligatory procedure, and if professional experts had found such prints, surely they would have made a comparison.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Because such a comparison would have assisted the authorities in confirming whether someone had held a weapon or not. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is exactly so. However, in this case, I think that such prints were not found, due to many reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, can you recall whether other persons who were detained in and around Ljuboten on the 12th of August were interviewed at other police stations?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There were persons in other police stations and all of those who were under suspicions or for whom there was indication that they directly took part in the fighting were interviewed and investigated.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Can we turn now to what is tab 4 in your binders, Your Honour. This is Exhibit P51, page 96. If you turn to the document that's at tab 4, Mr. Toskovski.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: This is an Official Note submitted by a man first initial B, last name Dejan, submitted to the Ministry of Interior, Cair, on the 13th of August, 2001. It's Official Note 536. Mr. Toskovski, is this person known as -- with the last name Dejan, was he a colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he was inspector in OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: The subject of this document is conducted official conversation with persons taken from Ljuboten village. And it describes conversations with nine persons at the OVR Kisela Voda, nine persons who been arrested at the Ljuboten village by the joint security forces. Mr. Toskovski, can you take a look at the third paragraph, please, begins with the phrase "one could hear shootings." Do you see that, third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: That paragraph reads: "One could hear shootings all over the place and there had been fights between the police of the Republic of Macedonia and terrorist gangs. The above mentioned persons stated that they have noticed a lot of terrorists who had been fighting with weapons in their hands whereas they have not participated in the clashes. But they wanted to escape from the village or some of them wanted to surrender to the security forces because they had not taken part in the fights." Do you see what I just read to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the content of the third paragraph in Official Note 536 is quite similar to the content of the third paragraph of Official Note 535 that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall why the contents of these two Official Notes written by two different inspectors are so similar? Do you recall why?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know why, but I can guess, that perhaps the colleague who is younger used my Official Note, having in mind the fact that the statements were identical of all persons.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You're saying that all persons, dozens and dozens of persons arrested at Ljuboten on the 12th of August, gave identical information to different police inspectors after their arrest. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, the information given by these persons in the interviews were, in principle, so to say, identical, not literally, but same justifications, same words were used, that they do not know, that they have not seen anything, that they had not taken part.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall why it was important that this -- that these notes be produced quickly? Do you recall why?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Because the time-frame is limited. The time-frame in which the police forces have to finish their work and if they were to have proof, evidence, to submit an adequate and necessary act, document.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall being told by your superior that the content of the conversations made at different locations with arrested persons should be recorded as more or less the same. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. Nothing like that was said.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Would you open up your statement, please, Mr. Toskovski, paragraph 49, please. Do you see paragraph 49?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Paragraph 49 says this: "Both documents have been produced on the next day," that would be the 13th of August "upon the order of my superior Krstevski like I mentioned before. He told us that there is not enough time and that the content of the conversations made at three different places should be more or less the same. I think my colleague simply took over the content from my document. That is the reason why they are looking all the same. All together, conversations have been made at Mirkovci station, Kisela Voda and Karpos. On Monday evening, I also visited the arrested persons at Karpos and Kisela Voda." Does this help to you recall what the circumstances were in the production of these Official Notes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: What -- I'm looking at what is written here. The order of my superior, Krstevski, perhaps we misunderstood each other, did not pertain to the notes themselves, how to write the notes. It pertained to the fact of speeding up the procedure because we already had elements to submit criminal report, criminal charges. This implies that we speed up the writing of the notes, among them these two, and everything else which is necessary to be written in this regard.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So that's why your colleague Mr. Dejan, apparently, took the contents of your note and placed it in his note, 536. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot claim this in his name. Perhaps this is so.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You were working under a lot of pressure at that time, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What kind of pressure are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You had to work quickly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Quickly, yes, we had to work quickly. But no one put any pressure on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we turn to tab 5 in your binder, Your Honours. This is Exhibit P50 at page 122.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: If you turn to tab 5, Mr. Toskovski. And take a look, please, at the Macedonian version. This is Official Note number 538, submitted by Blagoja Toskovski on the 14th of August, 2001. Subject conducted official conversation with persons taken from Ljuboten village. And here -- and if you -- can you see your signature on the bottom, Mr. Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Is this a note that you produced?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So this note records conversations that you had in Kisela Voda and Karpos with eight persons who were arrested at Ljuboten village. And take a look at the second sentence. In the middle -- excuse me, the second paragraph, in the middle it says: "Whereas in relation to the events, they stated the following. In the village one could hear shootings all over the place. And the above mentioned persons had seen that there had been fights between the police of Macedonia and terrorist gangs." In the next paragraph it says: "The above mentioned persons stated that they have also noticed a lot of terrorists who had been shooting with weapons in their hands whereas they had not participated in the clashes but they wanted to escape from the village after the security forces had entered into it." Do you see what I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Would you agree that the content of Official Note 538, information provided there allegedly by the interviewed persons is quite similar to the information provided in notes 535 and 536?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And do the same reasons apply?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes, the same explanation I gave that the statements were almost identical with the same explanation applies. This is why this is so.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I see. Again, you interviewed each person alone. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Had you ever, in your experience as a police officer, individual -- interviewed dozens of persons individually and received exactly the same information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Can you recall, Mr. Toskovski, whether then criminal charges were produced -- actually, let me -- let me step back for a moment. Apart from the information that is recorded in these Official Notes, Mr. Toskovski, did you get any other information on the 12th, 13th of August, 14th of August, about the circumstances of the arrest of these persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I obtained additional information from police officer, Sasa, I believe, was his name, from police station Mirkovci who took these persons over from the village.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please turn to what is exhibit number P23, please. It's tab 1 of your binders, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Turn to tab 1. Not your statement, please, Mr. Toskovski. Tab 1 in that binder of materials that you've got.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, if this exhibit was exhibited under seal, if it cannot be shown to the public, please.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, you see this is an Official Note submitted by Mr. Sasa on the 12th of August, 2001. It's Official Note 1131. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And in it Mr. Sasa talks about how on the 12th of August, he took over ten persons and some weapons and ammunition from the security forces of Macedonia at Ljuboten village. And then below that we see the names of the person who Mr. Sasa took over and the weapons and ammunition that Mr. Sasa transported. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So was this the information that you referred to a moment or two ago, that you received from Mr. Sasa, the additional information that you received about what had transpired at the arrest of these ten individuals?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have spoken with Sasa several times, and after this Official Note I had also had another conversation with him about the conversation. It is not just this one then.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Those conversations, did they discuss the persons who Sasa had transported on the 12th of August and the weapons and ammunition that Sasa had transported? Was that what you discussed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sasa give you any other information that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. No additional information other than which we see here and which he wrote.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Toskovski, can you recall whether criminal charges were produced regarding the persons who were arrested at Ljuboten; for example, the ten persons who you spoke with at Mirkovci police station. Were there criminal charges drafted?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, criminal charges were submitted.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And who drafted them?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I prepared these.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And can you recall whether you were given instructions to draft the criminal charges in a particular way?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. In which -- what do you mean "instructions"?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Were you given any instructions related to the drafting, the production of these criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: There's no need for any particular instructions to be given to me. In accordance the legal regulations, I know how to prepare them. Perhaps certain consultations can be carried out with the superior.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And you would -- you would include in criminal charges information that you had received up to that point about possible crimes that had occurred. Is that -- is that the correct procedure?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the question? I do not understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: When you draft criminal charges, in those documents to support the charges you would include information that you have received about the events, about the crimes that occurred. Is that right? Is that your procedure?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we take a look, please, at Prosecution Exhibit 31. Your Honours, it's at tab 16 of the binder that you have.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, these are criminal charges from the department of the interior for Cair, unit of operational affairs Cair, dated 13th of August, 2001. And if you turn -- if you look at the first and second pages, you'll see that the persons mentioned here, the ten persons, are actually the same persons who you describe in your Official Note 535. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So were these the criminal charges that you drafted with respect to these ten persons who were first detained at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: If you take a look, please, at the bottom of the second page in the English version, and it's also the bottom of page 2 in your version, in the Macedonian version. There's a paragraph at the bottom that says this -- and this is a description of the criminal act of terrorism or the preparation for the criminal act of terrorism. It says: "Namely, on the 12th of August, 2001 in the early morning hours the identified persons prepared the fire-arm they had provided previously and then in the time about 8.00 they were ready to start a direct attack to the positions of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia who were deployed in the area of the village of Ljuboten. These operations were undertaken with the aim to eliminate security forces and to endanger the constitutional order and security of the Republic of Macedonia." Do you see that, what I just read to you, I guess, this paragraph that you drafted on the 14th of August -- excuse me, the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Tell us please, this information that these ten persons were ready to start a direct attack on the positions of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia with the goal to eliminate them, tell us, please, where does this information come from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It comes from other previous information.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Toskovski, you've outlined to us the previous information that you've received. You've told us what the ten detained persons told you, and you've told us about the information that you received from Mr. Sasa. This information is not in Official Note 535. So tell us, please, where did -- where does this information come from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: This information comes from the services for state security and our police officers that obtained information on previous days.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I see. Your police officers -- you say "our police officers who obtained information on previous days." Which police officers obtained this information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not know their names.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: These unknown police officers, who did they speak to? Where did they get their information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: With their operative positions for which, I think, the analytical service had information.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I see. And the information that these other police officers obtained, where is it recorded prior to the 13th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not know. But it should be in the analytics sector. That's where they all flow in.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Very well. Take a look, please, at the top of page 4 in the English version, which is at page -- page 3 of the Macedonian version, top of page 3. There's another paragraph. It says -- are you with me? I'm sorry, this is tab 16, Mr. Toskovski, tab 16 of the same document, your criminal charges. Can you turn to page 3, please, in your version. At the top of page 3 it says: "The afore-identified persons continued with these operations until 12.00 when they deserted their combat positions. And they left fire-arm and equipment, actually, they threw away part of the equipment. All these, they did it in an order to avoid liability for the terrorist activities they had committed." Where does this information come from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: From security forces who were on the ground where the place -- where the events happened.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You see, what you told us a short time ago is that prior to drafting these notes, the only information you had received was information from Mr. Sasa and the information that you received by speaking with these ten persons. So how is it that you were able to put this information in your criminal charges on the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In preparing the charges, all possible information are collected and evidence are collected from all services, and are used in the preparation of the charges.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, that makes sense, except that you had told us earlier that you had not received any additional information. So I'm just trying to understand how this information found its way in the criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Just previously you asked me about additional information from the police officer Sasa, strictly from him, whether I received additional information. This is why I said what I did.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: No. I asked you whether apart from that, apart from the information from Sasa and from the information provided by the arrested persons, whether you had received any additional information. At that time your answer was no. Had you received further information before you drafted these criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is a misunderstanding. I thought this only pertained to Sasa, or so the question was formulated.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. You had mentioned earlier that you had produced seizure certificates or certificates for weapons and ammunition that had been seized from the ten persons who were detained at Mirkovci. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to what is tab 6 in your binder, Your Honour. This is Exhibit P46, page 46.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, do you see your signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: It's a certificate on temporary seized possessions dated the 12th of August, 2001. And this particular certificate relates to a gentleman named Bajrami Nevaip. Is this one of the seizure certificates that you produced during your discussion with this individual?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And it says here that an automatic rifle of Chinese production was seized. If you look at the first paragraph where the information about the person is given, the name, date of birth, village of Ljuboten, et cetera, it then says: "The authorised person," and there's a blank, there's no name "seized the following possessions in temporary custody." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So you don't know who seized this weapon, do you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, the name of the person, the name of the authorised person who seized the possession is not -- is not written here; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So can we take from that that at the time you didn't know who specifically seized this weapon, did you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You did not. You did not know the person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: According to the information I received at Mirkovci, from the people, from the state security and from Sasa, it all pointed to the notion that it was the security forces who seized this specific weapon and where and how I --

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, I cut you off. You meant to say where and how I? Can you finish the sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Where precisely, at what location in the village, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And you also don't know who precisely took possession of the weapon, do you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: So down below we also see it says: "The listed possessions are subject of," and below we see what is supposed to be written there is the grounds for which objects were seized. And there's nothing written there. And I just wanted to explore this with you, Mr. Toskovski. So at the time when this seizure certificate was produced you didn't know the circumstances, the specific circumstances that led to the seizure of this weapon, did you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I knew the specific circumstances. I didn't know the persons.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, all right. You see, you didn't write anything about the specific circumstances in this section. Can you tell us, please, now what were the specific circumstances in which a rifle was seized by Mr. -- from Mr. Nevaip Bajrami, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was given information that it was done at the actual scene of the events, of the combat activities in the village.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: But you have no more information than that.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn now, please, to what is tab 14. And, Your Honours, this is it Prosecution Exhibit 30.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Toskovski, is another certificate on temporary seized possessions dated the 12th of August, 2001. Do you see your signature there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you produce this certificate?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: This is a certificate that, on the 12th of August, ten bullets for an automatic rifle were seized from someone named Bajrami Mevludin. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Again, the authorised person who seized the following possessions is not named there. Does that mean you don't know who precisely seized this ammunition?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know. The same as in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And down below where it says the stated possessions are subject of and the grounds on which the objects were seized, again, there is nothing written there. Does this mean that you had no precise information as to the circumstances in which these bullets were seized from this individual?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I had no information, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the persons whose names -- whose signatures appear on these certificates, do you recall whether each person willingly signed them?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they willingly did.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Would it help you to refresh your memory about this point by looking at your statement? Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me try.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Take a look at paragraph 40 of your statement, please. Do you have paragraph 40 in front of you? Mr. Toskovski, do you have paragraph 40 --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: In the middle of paragraph 40 you say: "The only documents which was signed by these persons in my presence was documents that stated that objects have been seized by them. These were stating that the weapons and ammunition is taken from them. I asked them where these weapons are from. They deny that they were belonging to them. But they were signing the documents that the weapons were seized. They don't have to sign, in the case they would refuse, the police officer would sign." In this situation, did any of these persons refuse to sign?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. They did sign all the documents themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: My question is -- let me state my question a bit differently. Did each of these persons willingly sign their certificate?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Each of the persons signed the document willingly. Just one clarification, if I may. As you said earlier, if some of the persons does not sign the document, then it would be the police officer signing the document. That is a technical mistake; it is not the police officer signing. I had clarified in that interview that there is a legal possibility for the authorised officer who is running the interview if there are reliable elements, evidence, that the object does belong to the suspect, or that it is found on the suspect, and the person refuses to sign the certificate for temporary seizure of objects, then the authorised officer can enter a note clarifying that the person refuses to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. But in this case, what you're telling us is that each of the ten persons that you interviewed willingly signed their certificate. That's right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
