utterances.text: Can you think of a good reason why someone would first tell you that they did not have weapons in their possession but then would sign a certificate saying that they had weapons or ammunition in their possession, why they would do that willingly?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: After you present them -- after I had presented the arguments to them, they had signed. Am I clear, or should I clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Yes. Please clarify.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: During that brief interview, I explained to them that there are arguments and which are those arguments, that they were found on the spot that they themselves were found there, that they were handed over from there together with the weapons, that the paraffin glove test was positive for them, after which, without any discussion, they would sign.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, are you -- is it your testimony that you told these arrested persons in the early morning hours of the 13th of August that paraffin glove test results had been returned and that they were positive? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not remember actually whether I said something like that to them on the 13th, but on the 12th, during the interview, I might have pointed this to them, because we already had the initial information. Then I had indicated this to them.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: You had information that the so-called paraffin glove test had been performed, right? Because those tests --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Those tests were performed on the night of the 12th and 13th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And are you saying in the early morning hours of the 13th, you already had the results of those tests?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I just received them over the phone. I still hadn't have them in writing.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please go to --

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that although these persons told you that they weren't involved in combat and did not have weapons, that they -- upon listening to your arguments, they decided to sign these certificates?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to what is Exhibit P261. This is tab 17 of your binder, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, this is an Official Note, number 537. It is submitted by you. Do you see your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: It's dated the 14th of August, 2001. And it's called: "Subject report on a deceased person." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And it's talking about a gentleman named Atulla Qaili who was one of those ten persons detained at Mirkovci on the evening of the 12th of August. And it says in the second paragraph: "He was held at the Mirkovci police station from 0200 hours on the 13th. On the same day, at about 0430 hours, as his health condition deteriorated, the duty officer at the Mirkovci police station called the ambulance and he was taken to the Skopje city hospital." Then there's a sentence that says this is: "On the 13th of August, 2001, the Skopje city hospital informed us that the aforementioned person had died during the day." Do you see that, Mr. Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you do any investigation into the cause or the circumstances of the death of Mr. Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it? I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you do any investigation into the cause or the circumstances of the death of Mr. Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: We, and among those we, I myself, with the authorised officers have the duty to always work on clarifying the cases. Since a death had occurred in this specific case, the homicide department would be involved.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you know what steps, if any, the homicide department took to investigate the cause or circumstances of the death of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know specifically nor in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. It was my goal to finish my direct examination with this witness, but I need another five to ten minutes, so if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We allowed you to run on, thinking you were following a particular line. In retrospect, that was not so, but that is why we stretched this session. We will resume at a quarter past six.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, before we took the last break, I had asked you some questions about when you received results of the so-called paraffin glove tests for gunpowder analysis. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: You're referring to the written text or ...

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, do you recall the discussion that you and I had some moments ago.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving some information that the results of the tests for the ten persons who were detained in Mirkovci could not be produced because of contamination. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I don't know of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is P150, page-- I think that's probably a mistake. It should be P50. Yes, P50, page 135. This is at tab 20 of your binders, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: This is a report submitted by you, Mr. Toskovski, on the 31st of August, 2001, number 593. Do you see your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: It's a report on the events and undertaken measures at the area of Ljuboten village in the period between 10 August 2001 till 13 August 2001. And it contains some information about the events from 10, 11, and 12 of August. And then at the bottom it says: "In the military activities, the joint security forces had destroyed the terrorist groups who withdrew from the village towards Tanusevci and Kumanovo." And then it says: "Some of the terrorists were throwing weapons and escaping towards Radisani and Skopje." And then it says: "In total, 70 persons were arrested." Do you see that, Mr. Toskovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Can you recall why you drafted this report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this report was prepared by me at the request of the superiors in connection with the investigation that was led afterwards for the events and activities of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: When you say "the events and the activities of the police forces," you're referring to the activities of the police forces at Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And this investigation that you referred to, was it part -- was it due to a committee that Minister Boskoski had established at that time, to investigate these activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The information was requested about this, and I believe in the meantime it served for additional information to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. The information contained in your report, where did this information come from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Which information are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Well, all of it. I mean, where did you get the information that you put in this report. What were your sources?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It was my investigation after the events. That is to say, accruing and collecting all data and information that we had. That is to say, to which I was able to get.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of the police officers who were active in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you -- to gather the information that you put into this report, did you speak to any of the police officers who were active in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I spoke with Sasa. As for others, I did not do so. I used data from official records.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. So you didn't speak to a gentleman named Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not at all. I did not speak to him at all.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Did you speak to a gentleman by the name of Zoran Jovanovski, also known as Bucuk?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have not spoken to such a person.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. Did you find in the -- apart from speaking with Sasa and looking and -- from the data from the official records that you reviewed before you wrote this report, did you see any information indicating that some of the police officers in Ljuboten on the 12th of August might have overstepped their powers a little bit? Used --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have not seen such an information.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: All right. Any information that -- that the police officers active in Ljuboten on the 12th of August might have mistreated some civilians?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I have not seen such information.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And apart from this report, did you send any further reports to your superiors to be sent to this committee as part of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think, as far as I can recall, I did not prepare another report.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Okay. And did your superiors give you any comments when you sent your superiors this particular report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, there were no comments.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And did any members of the investigation committee established by Minister Boskoski, did any of them speak to you personally or ask you for information related to the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: They did not talk to me personally. However, this information was requested from my superior, from me, that it be submitted to the committee.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And after you submitted this information, you received no further comment about it from anyone?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: In any sense. Did any superior of yours in the Ministry of Interior talk to you about the report that you had sent to them?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: And did any of your superiors in the Ministry of the Interior request you to look for additional information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Without requesting it from me, I tried and all colleagues tried to get to additional, valid information that would clarify the case in full. However, we could not get to such information.

utterances.speaker: THE AMBULANCE MEDICAL TEAM
utterances.text: Do you think that speaking with the police officers who were involved in the operation in Ljuboten on the 12th of August might have helped you to clarify the situation, to clarify the case in full?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: I think this is what the committee did. This was within its competency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, while we put up the roster, I would ask the assistance of the court usher to help us to distribute to the Court, to the -- to my learned colleagues the files which -- with the documents which I intend to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Toskovski. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I am defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before -- before I proceed with putting some questions to you, which is possible to do in the course of this day, and others will follow in the course of next day, I would ask you for the following. You will probably understand the questions which I'm asking, and I understand the answers which you provide in the Macedonian language. However, both my questions and your answers must be translated. Therefore, -- and so the Honourable Court can follow as well as other colleagues in the courtroom. So I would ask you when you hear my question that you wait until it is translated and that -- respond only then. In this manner, we will be best able to assist Their Honours and the colleagues which are listening to this. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are by profession you are a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have graduated the faculty of law in 1984 in Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The question of my learned colleague, you said that from 1986 you worked and are working in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the work you worked in 2001, about which you have already testified, you worked in the unit for issuing ID and passports, and as of 1989, you work in the crime police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, one could say that in 2001, you already had 15 years of experience of working in the Ministry of Interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the unit of -- in the police -- in the interior in Cair, you were considered as inspector with substantial professional experience. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The question of the learned colleague you have explained that your concrete tasks and duties in 2001 were to work and to discover criminal acts against property, forgery, and other criminal -- and other property crimes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had the status of authorised person. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The competency of the Ministry of Interior in the Republic of Macedonia was established by law, although I would say that this is above all the Law on Internal Affairs, and in connection with the work which you carried out, and you carried out your duties and tasks this was also established by the Law on Criminal Procedure. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the law, would you agree with me that the books of rules and manuals, such as the Book of Rules on the organisation and organisational structure about the reserves of the police, awarding of weapons and so forth, that all of these secondary acts adopted by the government and some of them the minister, in effect, established the concrete duties and tasks, competencies of various organisational structures and also other questions, issues which are of importance for understanding the competencies and the tasks which you carried out. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These documents, in effect, established and determined which tasks are carried out by the Ministry of Interior on the level of the republic, that is to say the state, and which tasks of the bodies of the Ministry of Interior are carried out by regional organisational structures and bodies of the Ministry of Interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These, so to say, the centralised organs of the ministry in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001, they were founded or they were, in effect, sectors of the Ministry of Interior where most of the tasks of the bodies of the Ministry of Interior were carried out. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of the Ministry of Interior of Cair belonged to the sector of the interior of the city of Skopje. Is it correct that the sector of the interior of the city of Skopje had a larger number of organisational structures within the sector itself and a larger number of units of internal affairs in the municipality of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, five.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your unit of internal affairs in Cair, as well as the other units in other municipalities - you said there were five - composed of sections for operative work, your unit had two police stations, Cair and Police Station Mirkovci, and within the units there were also sections for analytics which in one of your answers you already mentioned. Is this the organisation of your unit?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally, you worked in the section for operative works. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in this section, crime police work was carried out, or, to be more precise, tasks of discovering crimes and perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To this part where you said consisted -- comprised your immediate task, detection and prevention of property crime. In the section, there were other parts which related to bodily harm or to homicides or delinquency, juvenile delinquency. You mentioned the colleague, the police -- the person who you met in the Police Station Mirkovci that she worked in this kind of issues; then, traffic misdemeanours. There were many tasks which your colleagues carried out within the sector. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood correctly, your immediate superior Mr. Ljupce Josevski was, in effect, the head of this operative sector, that is to say, all inspectors who worked in the area of detection of crimes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also I would ask you to tell me whether I understood you correctly that Ljube Krstevski was, in effect, the head or the chief of the overall unit where police stations, that is to say, Cair and Police Station Mirkovci, the unit of analytics and your operative section also belonged. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you just a while back whether it is correct that these tasks which you carry out, the real tasks and competencies established by Book of Rules and manuals, I would ask now that we look at this document which is found in tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is Exhibit 1D107, page of the Macedonian version, 1D4375 -- 71, my apologies, while the English is 1D4392.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is that the Book of Rules on the organisation and operation of the Ministry of Interior that was in force in 2001, taking into consideration some amendments to it done throughout the year. Was that the document on which you based your duties?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the final page of this document, that is the page 18. 1D4389 is the Macedonian version; and in the English version, that is the page 1D4413. Have you found this page?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can I draw your attention to the last element in this Book of Rules. You will see then that on the one side there is the number under which this document, Book of Rules is issued and the date, 26th of January, 2001, and on the other side, there is the signature of the minister of the interior who adopted, who passed this Book of Rules. Tell me, please, do you know -- actually, was Dosta Dimovska assigned -- who has signed on this Book of Rules, was she also a minister of the interior during one part of 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, she was minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell that you this Book of Rules as well as most of the general acts that you based your work upon in 2001, as well as the Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Criminal Procedure practically passed earlier and most of the regulation was in force for a number of years before Mr. Boskoski was appointed minister of the interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the Article 8 of this same Book of Rules. That is found in the English, page 4401; while in Macedonian 1D4379. Do you see this page now? That is the page 8.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you to look at the Article 8 first. And I will read to you the first sentence which says: "For the conducting of internal affairs on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, the following regional organisational forms of the ministry are established," and 11 such sectors are enumerated. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct if I say that these Articles precisely corroborate what you stated before, that the carrying out of all works or most of the works and affairs of the Ministry of Interior is done within the sectors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look now at the Article 9, you see there that the sector for internal affairs of the city of Skopje is the subject and its organisation and competences as well. I would like to ask you to look at -- you said that you were aware of this Book of Rules to see that in the first part, until item 12, that is actually the enumeration of the internal organisational forms within the sector for the city of Skopje, and then from item 13 to item 17, enumerated are the departments for internal affairs. Actually, the five departments that you spoke about, that you testified about earlier, departments or units?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in this last subitem, 17, you recognise your department for internal affairs, Cair, and you stated it comprised precisely those units that are enumerated here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look now at the Article 9 as a whole, would it be correct for me to say that actually all affairs of the bodies of the interior in the city of Skopje were divided to affairs carried out by the sector itself and affairs carried out by departments of internal affairs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And briefly again in relation to this, is it correct that practically all these affairs that we discussed from the beginning of my cross-examination of you are actually affairs that fall within the realm of affairs of public security?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And within the Ministry of the Interior there was also state security, isn't it so, that has a special organisation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These affairs of public security that were part of your tasks, wasn't it so in the municipality of Cair, were actually carried out through the uniformed police or to -- through the criminalistic police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague you briefly gave some data about the tasks you performed and you repeated those when asked by me, and I would ask you now a general question. Is the criminalistic police otherwise the one that carried out tasks related to prevention of crime, detection and apprehension of perpetrators, and also carried out other tasks that were otherwise prescribed in the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in relation to this answer and for the purposes of the transcript, I would like to state that these tasks are described in the Article 12 of the Law on Internal Affairs, which is the Exhibit P86.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, since we took a look at this Book of Rules and probably this is where we will end tomorrow -- today.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to you look at the provision of Article 21 and 22. It is found at page 16, 1D4387. And the English text is 1D4410. And the -- I would like to draw your attention to the first paragraph of Article 21 which states that certain organisational forms within the ministry and within the public security bureau as an organ within the structure of the ministry are headed by heads at a job and the title of whom is identified in the Law on Organisational Structure of the ministry, depending on the organisational form where they belong. Is your understanding as well, Mr. Toskovski, that each organisational form, and therefore your department for internal affairs, was actually managed by a head, whose tasks and responsibilities were established by this Law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at the Article 22 on the following page, you will see here that the heads of the organisational forms that are within the scope of another organisational form are directly responsible to the head of the respective organisational form. The employees direct performers are responsible before their immediate head and the head of the organisational form to which they belong for the correct execution of their works and tasks. Is such definition of the responsibility of actual responsibility of the direct performers and their heads something that was actually implemented in the practice, at the time when you worked at the department Cair, and especially during 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And apart from on the basis of the law, you also based your work on the annual and monthly plans that the unit adopted independently, and that was the absolute responsibility, legally prescribed responsibility of the department and the sector for the internal affairs. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to carry out your legal responsibilities, you didn't need any particular orders from the ministry or the Minister. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And within the line of command, the entire structure of the criminalistic police that you belonged to was headed by the under-secretary for criminalistic police and the bureau for public security actually completed the actual, the real competence of the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, considering that those were the organisational forms that actually carried out the competences of the Ministry of Interior prescribed by the law, I will finally ask you: Is it correct that, with regards to certain issues as specified in Article 25, it was possible to establish special committees or groups, task forces of permanent or provisional nature, tasked with certain issue, but such committees or groups could never replace the competences of the bodies, competences that belonged to the bodies under the law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So no committee could remove or modify the actual competences that you had as authorised officer or your head, who was the responsible person for the Cair department?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And such committees could not be a substitute for the work of the prosecutor's office or the courts to whom such competences and duties absolutely belong, as prescribed by the law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much. And I thank you for allowing me to complete with this Book of Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now for the evening, resuming tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
